intended_object: For a square matrix M over a commutative k-algebra Q and a scalar s ∈ Q, the k-subspace of vectors v ∈ kⁿ whose image in Qⁿ is an s-eigenvector of M, i.e. {v ∈ kⁿ : M·ι(v) = s·ι(v)}. These are the k-rational points of the s-eigenspace. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the `mem_rationalEigenspace` lemma.
explanation:
The body is the kernel of the k-linear map v ↦ (M.mulVecLin − s•id)(algebraMap ∘ v). Here `LinearMap.compLeft (Algebra.linearMap k Q) n` sends v to the vector algebraMap ∘ v in Qⁿ, and the scalars of the operator are restricted to k. A vector v lies in the kernel exactly when M *ᵥ ι(v) = s • ι(v). The simp lemma `mem_rationalEigenspace` states this, so the definition matches its docstring. Degenerate cases also behave as expected: if s is not an eigenvalue the space is ⊥, and if n is empty the space is the trivial space k⁰ = ⊤.

Mathlib has no direct counterpart. `Module.End.eigenspace` is a Q-submodule of Qⁿ, while this object is its preimage in kⁿ as a k-submodule, i.e. its rational points. One could write it as a `Submodule.comap` of a scalar-restricted eigenspace, but Mathlib has no named declaration for it.

On generality: the body only needs k to be a commutative semiring. Assuming a field is still the standard setting for "k-rational" vectors and k-forms under scalar extension, and the companion spanning result is used over fields. So this is not a case where the definition should clearly be stated more generally. It is a correct, natural formalization.
